To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
FCS-MPC can be used to control a grid-connected voltage source converter (VSC).

FCS-MPC can be applied in a multivariable way and that it is a suitable control method for grid-connected VSCs with an LCL output filter, as it enables a reduction in both switching losses and harmonic current distortion at a time.

finite control set model predicitive control (FCS MPC) can be used for multivariable control of grid-connected voltage source converters (VSC) and that the use of different state feedbacks and active damping methods can lead to different performance and robustness.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: (a) How to design a FCS-MPC controller for a grid-connected VSC with LCL filter?
the development of a control strategy for grid-connected converters with LCL filters, which can be implemented with low computational effort.
the development and implementation of a control strategy based on FCS-MPC for grid-connected VSCs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the FCS-MPC approach is a promising alternative to conventional control methods for the grid-connected VSC.

the FCS-MPC control strategy is a promising alternative to the widely used hysteresis current control (HCC), as it is capable of providing a similar performance with the advantage of a reduced switching frequency, which leads to reduced switching losses and lower harmonic distortion of the current.
FCS-MPC with multivariable control is the superior control approach for VSCs with LCL filters.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
FCS-MPC with multivariable control and active damping can be used as an alternative to classical control methods, especially for high-power applications.

FCS-MPC offers a promising alternative to classical controllers for VSCs with LCL filters.

the use of multivariable control in combination with FSC-MPC is a promising solution to control grid-connected converters with LCL filters, especially in the context of future power electronic applications.
